title: Screw jack
prompt: A labelled scale teaching model of the page 64 screw jack supports a miniature car load above a vertical screw in a fixed threaded pedestal. Crank turns the transverse handle and raises the screw and load by the thread lead. Reverse lowers them under controlled turning. Load changes the externally supported test weight, then compares the handle effort at the same geometry. See-through exposes the fixed internal thread, moving screw, handle and load contact. Show handle travel and load rise as overlays. Do not add scissor arms, a travelling nut linkage or a hydraulic cylinder.
blurb: A scale teaching model lifts a miniature car with a direct screw and compares ideal effort with handle travel.
truthNotes: Accepted scale teaching adaptation, not a literal book reproduction.
A rotating screw translates in a fixed threaded pedestal. No scissor arms, travelling nut or hydraulics.
Car and exchangeable roof weights are external teaching loads. Load doubles from 10 N to 20 N at fixed geometry.
Handle radius is 30 mm and lead is 3.769911 mm per turn. The ideal travel and force ratio is 50.
Ideal effort ignores friction. A stopped real jack relies on thread friction; controlled lowering is animated and has no free fall.
The load saddle swivels against the screw head so the car does not rotate.
Blue dashed paths are travel overlays, not physical hardware.
The board is a teaching fixture; motion is slowed for inspection.
1998 and 2016 saved primary page text and the 2016 page image were inspected. 1988 remains inaccessible and unverified. No edition union claim.
